initialConcepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create one exceptionally polished, full-viewport desktop WEB APPLICATION PAGE CONCEPT for The Seamless Cell. This is a visual design proposal to review before implementation, with original scientific illustration, not a scientific measurement or verified molecular structure. Landscape composition about 1536x1024. The application IS an immersive biological world, not a landing page or a dashboard. No device frame, browser chrome, collage, cards, promotional sections or Harvard/YouTube marks.
Art direction inspired by high-end educational molecular cinematography: the camera is situated INSIDE a dense three-dimensional biological landscape; tactile irregular folded protein surfaces, perceptible membrane layers, restrained translucent blue-teal membranes, pale lavender and moss-green molecular accents, occasional warm ochre. Soft blue-grey ambient depth, selective focus, realistic surface occlusion, strong near/middle/far layers, crisp selected subject, foreground partly out of focus. Shape carries meaning. Rich yet controlled colors, NOT monochrome brown, not neon, not glowing energy, not shiny plastic toys, not rainbow soup. Original composition, no copied video frame. Present illustrative morphology without implying atomic structural accuracy, exact organelle numbers, concentrations, or measured dimensions.
UI design consistent across a family of three screens: full bleed world occupies about 90% of the viewport. Very quiet thin typography in warm white; elegant modest serif wordmark 'The Seamless Cell' at top left. Small spatial breadcrumb at top center. At top right just 'Interphase' and 'Field notes'. UI supports the world rather than obscuring it. A discreet lower-left text region with a short serif subject title about 40px, one sentence in small readable sans serif, and two understated text tabs 'Structure' and 'Processes', active tab underlined; no heavy panel behind it. A single fine leader line can connect one small on-world label to its target, without giant circles. Bottom edge a fine divider and a sparse location/scale strip; no invented exact scale bars or numerical measurements. Tiny 'Visual concept' at bottom right. All UI is clearly separable for later code-native implementation. Legible copy, consistent alignment, generous margins, no invented extra labels or metrics. No biological motion trails or arrows unless specifically requested.
PAGE 1, Cell interior / STRUCTURE selected.
View from within a generic mammalian interphase reference cell, not an immune-cell scene copied from the reference. An impressive nucleus sits partly off-center in the middle distance, its irregular envelope and pore-like coarse surface details visible; broad folded endoplasmic-reticulum sheets extend around it in organic heterogeneous shapes, not concentric onion rings. A selected elongated curving mitochondrion occupies the right foreground/middle ground with a tasteful observer section revealing irregular inner-membrane folds while keeping its outer outline legible. Keep true organelle-scale visual composition; unresolved dense cytoplasm surrounds the structures. Slender cytoskeletal elements pass at different depths and help establish orientation, but no decorative giant molecular chains out of scale. No X-shaped chromosomes. The world should feel inhabitable and spacious enough to explore, with crowded organic context extending beyond the viewport.
Exact breadcrumb: 'Cell / Cytoplasm'.
Exact lower-left title: 'Cell interior'.
Exact sentence: 'Explore the structures that make up this cellular world.'
Tabs: Structure active, Processes inactive.
On-world label: 'Mitochondrion' with small linked action text 'Explore'.
Bottom-left: 'Reference cell · Interphase'; bottom-center: 'Organelle scale'.
Keep the upper-left and bottom-left quiet for readable interface while world details fill the center and right.

PAGE 2, Inside the mitochondrion / STRUCTURE selected.
The observer has entered the mitochondrion from the first page and is looking along its inner membrane from the matrix side. Build an extraordinary blue-teal crista landscape: undulating folded double-leaflet membrane sweeps from the lower-right foreground into the center distance and curves up like organic walls, with neighboring folds providing a sense of continuing compartment, not detached islands or a flat demo plane. A small observer section on one near fold reveals two leaflets with dense lipid head groups and inward hydrophobic tails. Surface layers must read as membrane architecture, not a pile of loose marbles. The actual inner-membrane architecture is an illustrative model, not a universal repeated accordion.
Several irregular coarse protein assemblies are embedded in this membrane landscape, muted lavender and grey-green. One selected ATP synthase dominates the right-middle foreground: its irregular multi-lobed matrix-facing catalytic head sits above the membrane on a slender central stalk, accompanied by a visibly separate curved peripheral stator connection, with membrane-embedded base. Use honest coarse protein-surface geometry, not invented atom coordinates or a generic metal machine. Its neighbors are less distinct, softened by depth. No literal glowing ions, no fluid stream, no energy beam.
Exact breadcrumb: 'Cell / Mitochondrion / Inner membrane'.
Exact lower-left title: 'Inside the mitochondrion'.
Exact sentence: 'Follow the inner membrane into a landscape of molecular machinery.'
Tabs: Structure active, Processes inactive.
On-world selected label: 'ATP synthase' with small linked action text 'Explore'.
Sparse environmental label on quiet upper left: 'Matrix'.
Bottom-left: 'Back to cell'; bottom-center: 'Molecular scale · schematic'.
The image must retain membrane and compartment context, not isolate a molecule in empty black space.

PAGE 3, ATP synthesis / PROCESSES selected.
Continue within the same blue-teal folded inner-mitochondrial-membrane landscape. A closer view of the selected ATP synthase sits in the middle-right, recognizable as the same multi-lobed muted lavender and moss catalytic head above an ochre slender central rotor stalk, with a distinct non-rotating peripheral support and membrane-embedded base. Protein surfaces should feel folded and molecular, not smooth primitive spheres, flowers, mushrooms, plastic, bolts or sci-fi turbines. The catalytic head projects into the MATRIX above the inner membrane; the opposite lower side is the INTERMEMBRANE SPACE. Include both sides of a local observer-sectioned lipid bilayer in the lower/mid frame, with nearby assemblies fading into the folded membrane background. Preserve sense of place, adjacency and depth, rather than presenting a disconnected protein model. No artificial glow. No arrows implying that electrons flow through ATP synthase. No invented count of H+ per ATP, rate, timeline duration or universal yield. Any structure is illustrative surface concept, not experimentally retrieved coordinates.
Exact breadcrumb: 'Cell / Mitochondrion / ATP synthase'.
Exact lower-left title: 'ATP synthesis'.
Exact sentence: 'Explore how proton movement couples to ATP production.'
Tabs: Structure inactive, Processes active.
Beneath tabs, one modest outline button with a small play icon and exact text 'Play sequence', and adjacent quiet text 'Biology paused'.
Two understated environmental labels 'Matrix' above membrane and 'Intermembrane space' below membrane.
One small on-world label 'ATP synthase', thin leader line.
Bottom-left: 'Back to inner membrane'; bottom-center: 'Molecular scale · schematic'.
The controls are proposed interface, not a claim of a running simulation. Keep the process UI extremely minimal and legible.

The attached image is the edit target and the visual source. Preserve the selected complex's recognizable shape: irregular lavender multi-lobed head with a pale blue central/front region, lavender central stalk, green peripheral stator on the RIGHT. Preserve these colors and the same molecular identity; do not substitute another protein shape. Preserve its right-of-center placement, perhaps enlarge it only about 15%, maintaining membrane and crista background landmarks. The matrix-facing head stays ABOVE the blue bilayer; the membrane-embedded base must sit IN the membrane, not float above or below it. This remains illustrative coarse geometry, not experimentally resolved atomic coordinates.
Preserve the luminous misty blue-teal environment, tactile folded surfaces, pale lavender/green restrained palette, selective depth of field, foreground occlusion and cinematic realism. Keep the recognizable winding membrane backdrop. Keep the existing lipid surface texture and a clear local section with one lipid bilayer: two facing leaflets, heads on the aqueous sides, hydrophobic tails facing inward, no accidental second bilayer added to the local section.
Keep the exact top-left wordmark 'The Seamless Cell', top-right 'Interphase' and 'Field notes', quiet serif/sans typography and overall layout. Change the top breadcrumb to 'Cell / Mitochondrion / ATP synthase'. Replace lower-left subject title with 'ATP synthesis'. Replace its description with 'Explore how proton movement couples to ATP production.' Place the Structure/Processes tabs under the description: Structure inactive, Processes active with thin underline. Under these tabs add one discreet outline button with small play icon and exact label 'Play sequence', and beside it 'Biology paused'. It is proposed UI in a static visual concept, not a running simulation. Move this lower-left content up enough to fit without crowding the bottom strip.
Retain one fine leader line and label 'ATP synthase', but remove 'Explore' from that label because this view has already selected the assembly. Keep environmental label 'Matrix' above the membrane and add 'Intermembrane space' below it in a clear quiet area. Bottom strip left: 'Back to inner membrane'; center: 'Molecular scale · schematic'; right: 'Visual concept'.
No glow, electron arrows, molecule streams, invented counts, rates, calibrated scale bars, atom positions, numerical time or new widgets. Do not change the visual language or turn it into a card dashboard. Preserve a full-page 1536x1024 landscape screen.
